question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the sentence given below.
Richa was provoking her neighbours against her maid Shanta who spoke against her but none of them responded.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Egging on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Egging on" means to encourage or provoke someone, usually to do something reckless, wrong, or against their better judgement. (किसी को उकसाना)
◦ Example: His friends egged him on to jump into the river despite the danger.

• In the given sentence, Richa was provoking her neighbours against her maid, i.e., she was instigating/inciting them — this is precisely what "egging on" means.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Smelling a rat (शक होना): To suspect that something is wrong or dishonest is happening.
◦ Example: When he avoided eye contact, I began smelling a rat.

• Option 3: Carrying the conviction (विश्वास दिलाना): To be convincing or persuasive enough to make people believe something.

• Option 4: Rising like a phoenix (राख से पुनर्जीवित होना): To make a strong comeback or recovery after a total failure or destruction, like the mythical phoenix bird rising from its own ashes.

NOTE

• Other idioms of instigation/encouragement often asked in SSC: "To incite", "To goad someone into", and "To fan the flames" (to make a bad situation worse).

• Do not confuse "egging on" (to provoke) with "to egg someone" in the literal sense (to throw eggs at someone) — in idiomatic use it always means encouragement toward a usually unwise action.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The chubby player was clearly told to bring his corpulent body into a good shape.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rotund.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Corpulent" means fat, plump, or having a large, bulky body. (मोटा/स्थूल)
◦ Example: The corpulent man found it difficult to climb the stairs.

• "Rotund" also means plump or rounded in shape, making it the closest synonym of "corpulent" among the given options. (गोल-मटोल)
◦ Example: The rotund gentleman waddled slowly across the room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "lanky" means tall and thin, often in an awkward way — this is nearly opposite in meaning to "corpulent".

• Option 3: "deformed" means abnormally shaped or disfigured, which is not the same as being overweight.

• Option 4: "plush" means luxurious or richly furnished, and has nothing to do with body shape.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "corpulent": obese, portly, stout, fleshy, burly.

• Antonyms of "corpulent": lean, lanky, gaunt, slender, skinny — a frequently tested antonym pair in SSC vocabulary questions.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A)Human relationships are a matter of great concern for every one of us.
B)Nevertheless, social scientists have attached many other elements that actually help us for a good social life.
C)As it helps us all to have a coordinated, balanced and approachable life.
D)The present generation fails to take cognisance of all such elements and fall prey to a lonely life risking happiness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ACBD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A is the clear opening/topic sentence — it introduces the subject of the paragraph, "human relationships", in a general way.

• Sentence C logically follows A because the pronoun "it" in C refers back to "human relationships" mentioned in A, explaining WHY relationships are a matter of concern — "as it helps us all to have a coordinated, balanced and approachable life."

• Sentence B then introduces a contrast using the connector "Nevertheless", shifting from relationships alone to the fact that social scientists have identified "many other elements" that also help a good social life.

• Sentence D concludes the paragraph, referring back to "all such elements" (the elements introduced in B) and stating that the present generation ignores them, resulting in loneliness.

• Applying this logical chain: A → C → B → D, giving the sequence ACBD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ADBC) is incorrect because placing D right after A is illogical — D refers to "all such elements", but no "elements" have been introduced yet at that point in the paragraph.

• Option 2 (DABC) is incorrect for the same reason — it opens with D, which refers back to elements that have not yet been mentioned, making the paragraph incoherent from the very first sentence.

• Option 3 (ABCD) is incorrect because starting B immediately after A with "Nevertheless" creates an abrupt, unjustified contrast — at that point A has not yet explained why relationships matter, so there is nothing for "Nevertheless" to contrast against.

NOTE

• In para-jumble/sentence-rearrangement questions, always locate the opening sentence first (usually a general statement introducing the topic, without pronouns referring back to something), and then trace pronoun references (it, such, these, that) and connectors (nevertheless, however, therefore, but) to fix the logical order.

• Sentences beginning with a demonstrative reference ("such elements", "this", "these") can never be the opening sentence of a paragraph.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Tourists from all around the world visit Agra to see the Taj mahal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Far and wide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "Far and wide" means over a large area; from/to many different places, everywhere. (दूर-दूर तक/हर जगह)
◦ Example: News of the discovery spread far and wide within hours.

• In the given sentence, tourists visiting Agra come from "all around the world", i.e., from everywhere — this matches the meaning of "far and wide" exactly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Ever and anon" (बार-बार/समय-समय पर): means now and then; occasionally, repeatedly — refers to frequency, not geographical spread.

• Option 2: "Cut and dried" (पहले से तय): means already decided or settled in a routine, unoriginal way; it has nothing to do with location.

• Option 3: "Few and far" (विरले/कभी-कभार, from "few and far between"): means rare, not happening or occurring often; again a matter of frequency, not geography.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "far and wide" (everywhere, geographical spread) with "few and far between" (rare in occurrence) — both contain "far" but mean very different things and are commonly used as distractors for each other in SSC papers.

• Other phrases of universality: "the world over", "from every corner", "from all walks of life".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
When will the results of the dance competition be announced?
option_1: When will they are announcing the results of the dance competition?
option_2: When will they announce the results of the dance competition?
option_3: When will they announced the results of the dance competition?
option_4: Will they announce the results of the dance competition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. When will they announce the results of the dance competition?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "When will the results of the dance competition be announced?" is a passive voice interrogative sentence in the Simple Future Tense, since the doer of the action (the agent) is not mentioned, and an indefinite pronoun "they" must be introduced as the subject in the active voice.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense (WH-question, passive → active):
◦ Passive: WH-word + will + Subject + be + V3 + (by + agent)?
◦ Active: WH-word + will + agent(they) + V1 + Object?

• Applying the rule: "be announced" (passive form) becomes "announce" (V1, base form) in the active voice, with "they" as the newly introduced subject, keeping the "When will" structure and the object "the results of the dance competition" unchanged.
◦ Active: When will they announce the results of the dance competition?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will they are announcing" mixes the future auxiliary "will" with the present continuous form "are announcing", which is grammatically wrong — two different tense auxiliaries cannot be combined this way.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "will they announced" wrongly uses the past participle/past form "announced" after the future auxiliary "will"; after "will" the verb must be in its base form (V1).

• Option 4 is incorrect because it drops the "When", changing the sentence from a WH-question (asking for a specific time) into a simple Yes/No question, which alters the meaning of the original sentence.

NOTE

• When converting a passive WH-question to active voice, always retain the WH-word at the beginning and introduce "they" (or an appropriate agent) immediately after the auxiliary verb.

• Common error: students often keep the verb in its "-ed"/V3 form after "will" — remember that after any modal (will, can, may, must), the main verb always stays in its base form (V1).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The old castle, with its towering walls, creaky gates, and secret passages, was the perfect example of a medieval fortress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. epitome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Epitome" means a person or thing that is a perfect example or embodiment of a particular quality or type. (प्रतिरूप/आदर्श उदाहरण)
◦ Example: The Taj Mahal is the epitome of Mughal architecture.

• In the given sentence, the old castle is described as the "perfect example" of a medieval fortress, which is exactly the meaning of "epitome".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "epicentre" (केंद्र बिंदु): the point on the Earth's surface directly above the origin of an earthquake, or more generally the central point of a difficult/dangerous situation — not a synonym of "perfect example".

• Option 2: "crux" (मूल बिंदु): the most important or decisive point of an issue or problem, e.g., "the crux of the matter" — refers to a core issue, not an ideal example.

• Option 4: "antithesis" (विपरीत/विरोधाभास): a person or thing that is the direct opposite of something else — this is actually opposite in meaning to "epitome".

NOTE

• Words close in meaning to "epitome": quintessence, embodiment, paragon, exemplar.

• Do not confuse "epitome" (perfect example) with "antithesis" (exact opposite) — SSC frequently pairs these two as distractors in the same question.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The __________ of the new legislation has sparked a heated debate among lawmakers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. effect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Effect" is normally used as a noun, meaning a result or outcome brought about by a cause. The blank requires a noun (preceded by "The" and followed by "of the new legislation"), so "effect" — meaning the impact/result of the legislation — fits correctly.

• Rule: "Affect" is almost always used as a verb, meaning to influence or produce a change in something, whereas "effect" is almost always used as a noun, meaning the result of such influence. (Affect = verb/cause; Effect = noun/result.)

• Applying the rule: "The effect [noun, result] of the new legislation has sparked a debate" is the grammatically and contextually correct sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "affectation" means an unnatural or pretended manner adopted to impress others, which does not fit the context of legislation at all.

• Option 2: "effection" is not a standard English word.

• Option 4: "affect" would require a subject and object structure as a verb (e.g., "The new legislation will affect lawmakers"); used here as a noun after "The ___ of", it is grammatically incorrect (its rare noun sense belongs to psychology, meaning "outward display of emotion", which is irrelevant here).

NOTE

• Memory trick: RAVEN — Remember Affect Verb, Effect Noun.

• "Effect" can rarely also be used as a verb meaning "to bring about" (e.g., "to effect a change"), and "affect" can rarely be a noun in psychology — but for SSC exams, stick to Affect = Verb, Effect = Noun.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Personel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Personnel" — meaning the people employed in an organisation or armed force.
◦ Example: All personnel must report to the main hall by 9 a.m.

• Spelling key: PERSON + NEL, with a double "N" — PER-SON-NEL. The given option "Personel" incorrectly drops one "n".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Appreciate" is correctly spelt — to recognise the value or worth of something.

• Option 2: "Passenger" is correctly spelt — a traveller in a vehicle who is not the driver.

• Option 3: "Complaint" is correctly spelt — a statement of dissatisfaction.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "personnel" (staff/employees, double "n") with "personal" (private, relating to a single person, single "n") — a very common SSC confusable pair.

• Other frequently tested double-letter spellings: accommodate, embarrass, occurrence, committee, questionnaire.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
She was not allowed for going outside by her mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. not allowed to go.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule: The verb "allow", when used in the passive structure "be allowed", must be followed by the infinitive (to + V1), not by a preposition + gerund ("for going").

• Correct structure: Subject + be (is/was/are) + allowed + to + V1 (base verb).

• Applying the rule: "not allowed for going" is corrected to "not allowed to go", keeping the passive sense of permission being denied.
◦ Corrected: She was not allowed to go outside by her mother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "not allowed to going" is incorrect because "to" here is the infinitive marker and must be followed by the base verb "go", not the gerund "going".

• Option 3: "not allowed by going" is incorrect because the preposition "by" does not fit after "allowed" in this sense; "by + gerund" indicates the means of doing something, which is not the intended meaning here.

• Option 4: "not allowing to go" is incorrect because it changes the passive voice (she is the receiver of the permission) into an active-like structure ("not allowing"), which distorts the original meaning and subject-verb relationship.

NOTE

• Verbs that are similarly followed by "to + V1": permit, allow, forbid, order, tell, ask, expect, want.

• Common error: students often use "for + gerund" after such verbs due to confusion with expressions like "famous for doing" — but allow/permit/forbid always take the to-infinitive.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Her determination impressed all of the other colleagues and inspires them to continue pursuing their dreams.
option_1: inspires them in continuing pursuing their
option_2: inspired them to continue pursuing their
option_3: inspires them to continue pursuing her
option_4: inspires them to continue pursuing there
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. inspired them to continue pursuing their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence has two verbs joined by "and": "impressed" and "inspires". Both actions happened at the same time and describe a completed past event, so both verbs must be in the same tense.

• Rule — Parallelism of tense: When two verbs describing the same time-frame are joined by "and", they must agree in tense. Since "impressed" is in the Simple Past Tense, the second verb must also be in the Simple Past Tense.

• Applying the rule: "inspires" (present tense) is corrected to "inspired" (past tense), giving: "Her determination impressed all of the other colleagues and inspired them to continue pursuing their dreams."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "inspires them in continuing pursuing their" is incorrect — it keeps the wrong present tense "inspires", and "in continuing pursuing" is an awkward, non-standard double-gerund construction.

• Option 3: "inspires them to continue pursuing her" is incorrect — besides the tense error, "her" (singular, referring to one female) wrongly replaces "their" (plural, referring to "the other colleagues"), causing a pronoun-antecedent mismatch.

• Option 4: "inspires them to continue pursuing there" is incorrect — besides the tense error, "there" (an adverb of place) is wrongly used instead of the possessive adjective "their".

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones: their (possessive) / there (place) / they're (they are) — frequently tested in SSC error-spotting and sentence-improvement questions.

• Whenever two clauses joined by "and"/"but" describe events in the same time-frame, always check that their verb tenses match.

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Do you obey your elders?
option_1: Are your elders obeyed by you?
option_2: Are you obeying by your elders?
option_3: Have your elders obeyed by you?
option_4: Do your elders obeyed by you?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Are your elders obeyed by you?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Do you obey your elders?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense (Yes/No question, active → passive):
◦ Active: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?
◦ Passive: Is/Am/Are + Object + V3 + by + Subject?

• Applying the rule: the object "your elders" becomes the subject; being plural, it takes the auxiliary "Are"; the verb "obey" becomes the past participle "obeyed"; and "you" becomes the agent introduced by "by".
◦ Passive: Are your elders obeyed by you?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "Are you obeying by your elders?" wrongly keeps "you" as the subject and uses the continuous form "obeying", which reverses the intended meaning (it now asks if the elders are obeying "you").

• Option 3 is incorrect because "Have...obeyed" is the passive structure of the Present Perfect Tense, not the Simple Present Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "Do your elders obeyed" mixes the present-tense auxiliary "Do" with the past participle "obeyed" without any "be" verb, which is ungrammatical for passive voice.

NOTE

• In passive interrogative sentences, the auxiliary verb (is/am/are/was/were) always comes first, followed by the object (now subject), then the past participle, and finally "by + agent".

• Always match the auxiliary verb's number (singular/plural) with the new subject — here "elders" is plural, hence "Are", not "Is".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
I can’t believe that you’re ________ (resolute) enough to not even decide what you want for dinner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. indecisive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Resolute" means firm and determined in purpose; having made up one's mind clearly. (दृढ़ निश्चयी)

• Its antonym, "Indecisive", means unable to make a decision quickly and effectively; wavering. (अनिर्णायक)
◦ Example: He was too indecisive to choose between the two job offers.

• The sentence itself supports this — the person is described as unable to "even decide what you want for dinner", which is the very definition of being indecisive, the opposite of resolute.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "reluctant" (अनिच्छुक): unwilling to do something — this describes unwillingness, not an inability to decide.

• Option 3: "disinclined" (अनिच्छुक/नापसंद): having a lack of desire or willingness to do something — again about unwillingness, not indecision.

• Option 4: "gullible" (भोला/आसानी से धोखा खाने वाला): easily deceived or tricked — unrelated to the idea of decisiveness.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "resolute": determined, steadfast, firm, unwavering.

• Other antonyms of "resolute": irresolute, wavering, hesitant, vacillating — "vacillating" and "indecisive" are frequently tested together as near-synonymous antonyms of "resolute" in SSC papers.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. We must not complain
B. thorns bear flowers
C. but rather be grateful that
D. that roses have thorns
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ADCB.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part A ("We must not complain") must open the sentence, as it introduces the subject and main verb of the sentence.

• Part D ("that roses have thorns") must follow A directly, since "complain" needs the conjunction "that" to introduce its object clause — "We must not complain that roses have thorns."

• Part C ("but rather be grateful that") follows next, introducing the contrasting idea with the connector "but rather", and itself needs another "that"-clause to complete its meaning.

• Part B ("thorns bear flowers") completes the sentence, serving as the object clause of "grateful that".

• Combining in this order: "We must not complain that roses have thorns, but rather be grateful that thorns bear flowers." — a well-known proverbial saying, giving the sequence ADCB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (ADBC) is incorrect because placing B directly after D — "...that roses have thorns, thorns bear flowers..." — leaves the sentence without the necessary contrasting connector "but rather be grateful that", making it ungrammatical and incoherent.

• Option 3 (ACDB) is incorrect because "We must not complain but rather be grateful that..." skips the object of "complain", making the first clause incomplete.

• Option 4 (ABCD) is incorrect because "We must not complain thorns bear flowers..." makes no grammatical sense — "complain" cannot be directly followed by "thorns bear flowers" without the conjunction "that roses have thorns" in between.

NOTE

• In sentence-part-rearrangement questions, look for words that must grammatically follow one another, such as a verb needing a "that"-clause (complain that / grateful that), before checking the overall meaning.

• This particular sentence is a well-known proverb — recognising common proverbs and idiomatic sayings can help solve such jumbled-sentence questions quickly.

question: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
option_1: I need to buy an new iPhone.
option_2: The cat sat on the windowsill
option_3: She is the best singer in the choir.
option_4: He is an artist who paints landscapes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I need to buy an new iPhone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Use of "a" and "an": The article "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, while "a" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound.

• The word "new" begins with the consonant sound /n/, so it must be preceded by the article "a", not "an".

• Applying the rule: "I need to buy an new iPhone" should be corrected to "I need to buy a new iPhone."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "The cat sat on the windowsill" is grammatically correct — a simple, complete Subject + Verb + Adverbial sentence (though it lacks a full stop, this is not a grammatical error of the kind tested here).

• Option 3: "She is the best singer in the choir." is grammatically correct — correct use of the superlative degree "the best".

• Option 4: "He is an artist who paints landscapes." is grammatically correct — "an" is correctly used before "artist", which begins with the vowel sound /a:/, and the relative clause "who paints landscapes" is correctly formed.

NOTE

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the letter, that follows: e.g., "an hour" (silent h, vowel sound) but "a university" (consonant /y/ sound despite starting with a vowel letter).

• Commonly tested cases: an honest man, a European trip, an MBA degree, a one-way street.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.
(Ø = No article)
____ year ago, Arihant decided to join ____ NCC.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A; the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule 1: The article "a" is used before singular countable nouns beginning with a consonant sound. The word "year" begins with the consonant sound /j/ (as in "yes"), so it takes "a", not "an" — hence "A year ago".

• Rule 2: Names of well-known institutions, organisations, and forces that are commonly referred to by their abbreviations are usually preceded by the definite article "the" — e.g., the NCC (National Cadet Corps), the UNO, the NDA.

• Applying both rules: "A year ago, Arihant decided to join the NCC."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "A; an" is incorrect because "NCC" is pronounced starting with the vowel sound "en", but as a proper institutional name it conventionally takes "the", not "an" — "an" is not idiomatically used before institution names like NCC.

• Option 2: "The; Ø" is incorrect because "year" here is a non-specific, first-mention singular countable noun, so it needs the indefinite article "a", not "the"; and "NCC", being a specific organisation, needs "the", not zero article.

• Option 3: "The; a" is incorrect because "year ago" (a general, first-mention time period) should take "a", not "the"; also "a NCC" is wrong because NCC begins with a vowel sound.

NOTE

• Zero article (Ø) is used before plural/uncountable nouns used in a general sense, and before most proper nouns (e.g., "India", "Monday") — but not before well-known abbreviated institution names, which usually take "the".

• Similar cases: the UNO, the UPSC, the SSC, the ISRO — but note some abbreviations like "NASA" or "UNESCO", being pronounced as words, may be used without an article in certain contexts; when in doubt for SSC, well-known government/defence bodies referred to by initials generally take "the".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The singer’s performance captivated the audience and left them mesmerised.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disillusioned.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Captivated" means to attract and hold the interest and attention of someone; to charm or fascinate. (मंत्रमुग्ध करना)

• Its antonym, "Disillusioned", means disappointed on discovering that something is not as good as one believed it to be; disenchanted. (मोहभंग होना)
◦ Example: After the scandal, many fans felt disillusioned with their once-favourite singer.

• Since "captivated" describes being charmed/fascinated, its opposite is being disenchanted/disappointed — i.e., "disillusioned".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Enthralled" (मंत्रमुग्ध): means captivated or fascinated — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "captivated".

• Option 3: "Horrified" (भयभीत): means feeling great horror or shock — this describes fear, not the specific sense of losing charm/interest that is the true opposite of "captivated".

• Option 4: "Resisted" (विरोध किया): means to withstand or refuse to accept something — unrelated to being charmed or fascinated.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "captivated": enchanted, spellbound, fascinated, mesmerised.

• Other antonyms of "captivated": bored, repelled, disgusted, disenchanted — "disillusioned" and "disenchanted" are commonly tested together as antonyms of words meaning "charmed".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Punctual
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Late.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Punctual" means arriving or doing something at the expected or agreed time; not late. (समय का पाबंद)

• Its direct antonym is "Late", meaning arriving or happening after the expected or usual time. (देर से)
◦ Example: He is habitually late for every meeting, unlike his punctual colleague.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Dependable" (भरोसेमंद): means reliable or trustworthy — this is actually closer in spirit to a positive trait like "punctual" rather than its opposite.

• Option 2: "Precise" (सटीक): means exact and accurate — unrelated to timeliness.

• Option 4: "Ready" (तैयार): means prepared for something — this does not mean the opposite of being on time.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "punctual": prompt, timely, on time, regular.

• Other antonyms of "punctual": tardy, unpunctual, dilatory — "tardy" is a frequently tested synonym of "late" in SSC vocabulary questions.

question:
Select the option with the correct spellings to replace the underlined words in the given sentence.
His charesmatic attitude is admirble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. charismatic; admirable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the first word is "Charismatic" — meaning having a compelling charm or attractiveness that inspires devotion in others. Spelling key: it begins with "CH" (pronounced as "k"), not "K" — CHA-RIS-MA-TIC.

• The correct spelling of the second word is "Admirable" — meaning deserving respect and approval. Spelling key: ADMIR(E) + ABLE; the silent "e" of "admire" is dropped before adding the suffix "-able", giving ADMIR-ABLE (not "admirble" or "admerable").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "karismatic; admerable" — incorrect; "karismatic" wrongly uses "K" instead of "CH", and "admerable" has the wrong internal vowel ("e" instead of "i") and is missing a letter.

• Option 2: "charismatic; admarable" — incorrect; "charismatic" is correctly spelt here, but "admarable" wrongly changes "admir(e)" to "admar".

• Option 3: "karismatic; admirable" — incorrect; "admirable" is correctly spelt here, but "karismatic" wrongly begins with "K" instead of "CH".

NOTE

• The word "charisma" and its adjective "charismatic" derive from Greek and always retain the "CH" spelling (pronounced /k/) — commonly confused with words that are genuinely spelt with "K".

• Rule for "-able" suffix: when a root word ends in a silent "e" (like admire, desire, adore), the "e" is usually dropped before adding "-able": admire → admirable, desire → desirable, adore → adorable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words/phrase.
Spoken or done without preparation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Extempore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extempore" means spoken or done without any preparation; impromptu. (बिना तैयारी के/तत्काल)
◦ Example: She delivered a brilliant extempore speech on climate change without any notes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Elocution" (वाक्पटुता/भाषण कला): the skill of clear and expressive speech, especially in public speaking — this refers to the manner of speaking, not the lack of preparation.

• Option 3: "Debate" (वाद-विवाद): a formal discussion in which opposing viewpoints are argued — usually prepared and structured, the opposite of impromptu.

• Option 4: "Declamation" (भाषण/पाठ): the act of reciting a piece of prepared, often rehearsed, dramatic speech.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often tested together: "Impromptu" (done without being planned in advance — synonym of extempore), "Verbatim" (word for word), "Ad-lib" (to speak without preparation, informally).

• Do not confuse "extempore" (without preparation) with "eloquent" (fluent and persuasive in speaking) — both relate to speech but test different qualities.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word from the following sentence.
Empowered
People feel liberated in modern democracies, yet it is believed they are enslaved in their minds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. enslaved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Empowered" means given the authority, power, or confidence to act and make one's own decisions; made free and capable. (सशक्त/अधिकार-सम्पन्न)

• Its antonym, "Enslaved", means made into a slave; deprived of freedom and personal power, kept under someone else's control. (गुलाम बनाया गया)
◦ Example: Blind superstition can leave the human mind enslaved even in a free society.

• Among the words used in the given sentence, "enslaved" (a state of being controlled and powerless) is the direct opposite of "empowered" (a state of having power and freedom).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "liberated" (मुक्त): means set free — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "empowered".

• Option 3: "minds" (मन): a plain noun referring to the human mind/intellect; it carries no meaning of power or its absence, so it cannot be an antonym.

• Option 4: "modern" (आधुनिक): means belonging to the present time; it is unrelated to the concept of power or freedom.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "empowered": enabled, authorised, liberated, emancipated.

• Other antonyms of "empowered": powerless, disempowered, oppressed, subjugated — "enslaved" and "subjugated" are often tested together as antonyms of words expressing freedom or authority.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

Communication is very important for us humans in our daily lives. It means talking to others, (1)_______________ our thoughts and feelings, and listening to what others have to say. When we communicate well, we can understand each other better and work together more (2)____________. Communication is especially important at work, where we need to work as a team and achieve common goals. Good communication helps us to avoid misunderstandings and (3)____________, and makes us more productive. In our personal relationships, communication helps us to express our feelings and needs to our friends, family and partners. When we communicate well, we can build stronger relationships and understand each other better. Communication is also important for society as a whole. It helps us to share information, ideas and knowledge, and to understand different cultures and (4)_________________. Communication can also help us to make positive changes in our communities and (5)_______________ for important causes. Overall, communication is a very important skill that we all need to learn and practice. It can help us in many different ways and make our lives more fulfilling and successful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. sharing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that communication "means talking to others, (1) our thoughts and feelings, and listening to what others have to say." The blank must logically parallel the ideas of "talking" and "listening", i.e., it should mean communicating/giving out one's thoughts and feelings to others.

• "Sharing" means to tell others about one's thoughts, feelings, or information, which fits perfectly in this context — talking to others, sharing our thoughts and feelings, and listening to what others say.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "modifying" means changing or altering something — this does not fit the idea of communicating one's thoughts and feelings.

• Option 3: "classifying" means arranging into categories or groups — irrelevant to expressing thoughts and feelings.

• Option 4: "converging" means coming together from different directions to meet at a point — it does not fit the act of expressing personal thoughts and feelings.

NOTE

• In cloze/fill-in-the-blank passages, always read the full sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) before choosing an option — words that are close in general meaning can still fail to fit the exact context and collocation used.

• "Share thoughts and feelings" is a very common collocation in English and frequently appears in SSC cloze-test passages about communication and relationships.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. effectively.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "When we communicate well, we can understand each other better and work together more (2)." The blank is an adverb modifying "work together", and logically should mean in a productive, successful manner, paralleling the earlier phrase "communicate well".

• "Effectively" means in a way that produces the intended or desired result; successfully, which fits perfectly — working together more effectively as a result of good communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "economically" means in a way that saves money or resources — the passage is about communication and teamwork, not financial savings.

• Option 3: "sufficiently" means to an adequate degree; while grammatically possible, it is vaguer and less precise than "effectively" in describing the quality of working together that results from good communication.

• Option 4: "vibrantly" means in a lively, energetic, or vivid manner — this does not logically describe the outcome of understanding each other better through communication.

NOTE

• When more than one option seems grammatically possible in a cloze test, choose the one that best matches the passage's overall theme and cause-effect logic — here, good communication logically leads to more "effective" teamwork, which is the passage's central idea.

• Common collocations: "work together effectively", "communicate effectively", "an effective team".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mistakes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Good communication helps us to avoid misunderstandings and (3), and makes us more productive." The blank must be a noun that pairs naturally with "misunderstandings" as something good communication helps us avoid at the workplace.

• "Mistakes" (errors made due to poor coordination or unclear instructions) logically pairs with "misunderstandings" — good communication at work reduces both misunderstandings and mistakes, thereby increasing productivity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "distractions" means things that divert attention — communication does not typically "avoid distractions" in the sense intended here; this does not fit as naturally as "mistakes".

• Option 2: "justifications" means reasons or explanations given to defend an action — avoiding "justifications" does not logically connect to productivity in the way the sentence intends.

• Option 4: "quizzes" means short tests — completely irrelevant to workplace communication and productivity.

NOTE

• The pairing "avoid misunderstandings and mistakes" is a very common expression in passages about workplace communication and teamwork — recognising such natural word-pairs (collocations) helps solve cloze tests quickly.

• Related vocabulary often tested together: error, blunder, lapse, oversight — all near-synonyms of "mistake".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. advocate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Communication can also help us to make positive changes in our communities and (5) for important causes." The blank must be a verb, parallel to "make positive changes", describing a positive action taken to support important causes.

• "Advocate" (used here as a verb) means to publicly support or recommend a particular cause or policy, which fits perfectly — communication helps us make positive changes and advocate for important causes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "propagate" means to spread or promote (an idea, doctrine, etc.) widely; while related in meaning, it is more commonly used with abstract ideas/beliefs and lacks the natural collocation "propagate for a cause" (the correct usage is "propagate a cause", not "propagate for").

• Option 3: "inoculate" means to protect someone from a disease by injecting them with a vaccine, or figuratively to protect someone against an unwanted feeling/idea — this is unrelated to supporting social causes.

• Option 4: "recommend" means to suggest something as being good or suitable; while plausible in isolation, "recommend for important causes" is not idiomatic, whereas "advocate for" is the standard, natural collocation.

NOTE

• "Advocate for" is a fixed, commonly used phrase meaning to actively campaign or speak in support of something (e.g., "advocate for human rights", "advocate for change") and is frequently tested in SSC cloze passages on social themes.

• Do not confuse the verb "advocate" (to support publicly) with the noun "advocate" (a lawyer, or a person who publicly supports a cause).
